essence: Melting and entry: same-sap minds dropping disaster, axes of certainty on passion's root, melting stain-strings (vv1-3).
Mother and ripening: wallowing fed sap on sap to sky-going, connoisseurship won, mind-jewel spark-shed (vv4-6).
Station won: full-throated hymning past waiting gods, whole-sensed seeing, wed mind-lad hardening mine-thought (vv7-9).

sections.SUMMARY: The mind is cured by drowning: dropped in the bliss-ocean (1), axed at the mine/not-mine root (2), melted then blazing (3), mother-fed till winged (4), skilled in tasting (5), sun-melted of wax-drops (6), praising where gods wait outside (7), seeing world-as-Śiva through frenzy (8), and finally remarried — the mind-boy wedding the devotion-maiden and hardening a new mine (9).

rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of victory (vijaya) over distress (vidhura); the vyabhicāri is courage (dhairya) of the mind's cure. The rasa is the tranquility of victory — domestic allegory making the mind's cure narratable.
